findings.text: The deprecated path now asserts `obj.(*Mock)` instead of `obj.(Mock)`. A caller passing a `Mock` value (`myMock.Mock`) no longer matches, so `obj.(assertExpectationser)` panics because the `Mock` value lacks pointer-receiver methods. Previously the value was converted to a pointer, so this was a regression.

The mutex is now a value field. Any code that copies a Mock, such as the old by-value `obj.(Mock)` path, copies the lock state. If the copy happens while the mutex is held, the copy is permanently locked.

raw:
The `AssertExpectationsForObjects` change breaks the deprecated path. A `Mock` passed by value (`myMock.Mock`) no longer matches `*Mock`, so the type assertion `obj.(assertExpectationser)` panics. Passing `*Mock` previously worked on its own, because `*Mock` implements the interface. Passing a `Mock` value now also copies the mutex, which `go vet` flags.

1.reason: The patch removes the by-value `obj.(Mock)` path (it becomes `obj.(*Mock)`), every method on Mock uses a pointer receiver, and a value `sync.Mutex` is the normal Go idiom, so no code path in the change copies a held lock; the real problem with by-value Mocks is the unchecked `obj.(assertExpectationser)` panic, not lock-state copying.
